subject: Renewal + midyear top-up alignment & tiered pricing options
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: 2026-07-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal pricing and midyear top-up options

Hi Vanessa,

We are kicking off our renewal conversation and want to understand options for both our upcoming annual renewal (Oct 1) and a potential midyear top-up if our Q4 pilot scales faster than expected. Key asks from my side:

- Can you share a clear pricing ladder for incremental capacity (per GPU-hour or token band)?
- Any mid-contract co-terming approach so we can align renewal date with other vendors?
- Discount bands / thresholds for committed growth vs on-demand usage.
- Procurement needs: standard SOW, PO timeline, SOC 2 evidence (we'll need a short summary).

We have a budget window in August for procurement approvals, so a concrete proposal this week would help.

Thanks—
Sarah Nguyen
Head of ML Platforms, PulseHealth

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and midyear top-up options

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. I pulled together three straightforward paths that balance predictability and flexibility; attaching a short workbook that lays out unit economics and a draft SOW. Summary here:

Option A — Annual commit (best unit economics)
- 25% discount vs on-demand at annual committed spend $X
- Co-term on Oct 1 (we can annualize any midyear top-up into the next invoice)

Option B — Annual commit + burst buffer
- 18% discount on committed units, plus a burst pool at 1.8x rate for spikes
- Mid-contract top-up can be added at the committed unit price for the remainder of term.

Option C — Consumption-first with locked thresholds
- No upfront commit; stepped discounts at usage bands (10%, 15%, 22%) as monthly usage passes thresholds
- Best for unpredictable spike-driven pilots; slightly higher unit cost than A.

Procurement & SOC2: attached SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf and the draft SOW (PulseHealth_SOW_v2.pdf). I propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the workbook and pick a preferred path—would 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PulseHealth pricing posture & negotiation points

Quick internal note before the call:

- PulseHealth has historically preferred annual commits but is price-sensitive around first-year discounts. We can offer a blended ramp: 20% year-1, 25% year-2 if they annualize top-up.
- For mid-contract top-ups, recommend we allow conversion of burst usage to committed units at a 10% uplift to the committed price (protects against churn while rewarding conversion).
- Approve offering a one-time onboarding credit (up to $8k) to offset integration costs if they sign by Aug 20.

Priyom — can you prepare a quick note on implications for capacity scheduling if they exercise burst => commit conversion midterm?

Ben
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@pulsehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com, Mike Park <mike.park@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-31T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and midyear top-up options

Thanks Vanessa — 10am PT tomorrow works. A couple of clarifications ahead of the call:

- Procurement timeline: we need the final SOW + price table to route a PO approval by Aug 18.
- SOC2: the summary looks good; can you confirm whether logs retention and audit evidence meet a 12-month retention minimum?
- Discount ask: We were hoping for something closer to 22% effective discount for year-1 if we commit to a 10% uplift on top-ups converting to committed units (i.e., lower initial discount but strong conversion credit).

If you can include a one-page mutual action plan in the drive before the call, that'll speed approvals.

Sarah

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing and midyear top-up options — mutual action plan + next steps

Sarah / team —

Great call today — appreciate the honest tradeoff discussion. Per our conversation, here's a concise mutual action plan to circulate to Procurement:

1) Commercial path selected: Option B (Annual commit + burst buffer) with blended Year-1 effective discount of 20% and Year-2 of 25% if they annualize top-up within the term.
2) Mid-contract conversion: Burst-to-commit conversion allowed at a 10% uplift to the committed unit price; conversion applies to remainder of term only.
3) Onboarding credit: $8,000 one-time credit applied to the first invoice if signed by Aug 20.
4) SOC2: logs retention confirmed at 12 months; SOC2 evidence folder: drive link (see above).
5) Docs for PO: PulseHealth_SOW_v2.pdf and a line-item pricing table (attached). Procurement should receive final SOW + price table by EOD Aug 3 to meet their Aug 18 PO window.

Attachments: PulseHealth_SOW_v2.pdf, pulse_pricing_workbook.xlsx, SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf

Next steps: Ben to prepare final commercial summary and legal to prepare amendment for signature. Vanessa to upload M.A.P. to the shared Drive and create HubSpot deal note.

Thanks — excited to keep this moving.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
